headline: Share what matters. Keep what matters.
keyMessage: It isn't meant to replace the places where we talk to each other. It's meant to preserve the things we don't want to lose.
problem: Conversations move on. Useful links get buried. Recipes, songs, documents, ideas and experiences become difficult to find.
purpose: Share & Learn gives those things a permanent home—together with the people and conversations that give them meaning.

flow.line: with the people it is meant for
so it does not scroll away
the way your group thinks about it
through what people say about it

why.heading: Why Share & Learn
paragraphs: We already share the good things with each other — a song somebody sang at a wedding, the recipe an aunt finally wrote down, a book that changed somebody's year, a remedy from a grandmother, a link worth reading twice.

And then it scrolls away. A month later it is somewhere in a group chat, under two hundred photos and a poll about a picnic, and the only way back to it is to ask whoever shared it whether they still have it.
Keep talking wherever you talk. When something comes along that shouldn't be lost, put it here — and it will still be here, findable, when somebody goes looking.

points.title: Circles hold the people
points.copy: A family, a temple group, a book club, a handful of friends. You share into one or more circles, and what you share stays with the people it was meant for. A circle can be private, ask to join, or open to all.

points.title: Folders hold the order
points.copy: Every circle arranges its own — festivals, weeknight dinners, whatever it actually needs, nested as deep as it likes — so a thing shared today is still where somebody would think to look for it next year.

points.title: Each kind keeps its own details
points.copy: Songs, recipes, books, remedies, words, fun facts and bookmarks. A song keeps its words and their language, a recipe its ingredients, a book its author — so nothing worth knowing has to be squeezed into a caption.

points.title: Conversations stay with the thing
points.copy: Discuss a book or a song, add your experience or a tip to a recipe or a remedy, offer a word in another language. What people say stays next to what it is about.

points.title: Easy to find again
points.copy: Search a circle, walk its folders, or save anything to your own library so it is there whenever you want it.

communities.heading: Built around communities
paragraphs: Every circle decides what it is for. A family keeps its recipes and remedies; a music group keeps its songs with their words; a temple group keeps the events and prayers it returns to every year; a book club keeps what it read and what it thought of it.
A circle can add categories of its own, shape the details each one asks for, and arrange its folders the way its members already think — so each community preserves its own knowledge in its own way.

closing: Share & Learn isn't meant to replace the places where we already talk to each other—WhatsApp, websites, email, or other communities.
It's a place to preserve the things we don't want to lose, organize them so they're easy to find again, and share them with the people we care about.
